newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish businessmen murder trial begins.
newsitem.headline: Turkish businessmen murder trial begins.

text.p: Eleven members of a leftist urban guerrilla group went on trial on Tuesday charged in connection with the killing last year of two prominent Turkish businessmen and a secretary.

Ercan Kartal, the alleged mastermind of the assassination, denied that he gave the order to two gunmen who shot dead Ozdemir Sabanci, head of the Toyotasa car joint venture and Haluk Gorgun, the firm's general manager, along with a secretary in January, 1996.
But Kartal, who was in jail when the killings took place, boasted about the assassination in an 18-page statement he read to the court, state-run Anatolian news agency reported.
"The action was carried out by going into a place about which the monopolists said there was no way in and no way out," he said.
A prosecutor was expected to ask for the death penalty for four of the defendants and jail terms of seven-and-a-half years for the others.
Six of Kartal's co-defendants were also present in court. Two others are in police custody but were not in court and two are at large.
The Revolutionary Peoples' Liberation Party-Front (DHKP-C), Turkey's most lethal armed far-left group, claimed responsibility for the killings at Sabanci Holding's twin towers in Istanbul.
Mustafa Duyar, who gave himself up to the Turkish embassy in Syria in January and confessed to being one of the killers, was not in court. He has been held in jail since being brought to Turkey.
The other alleged trigger-man and a woman who is accused of helping the two gunmen breach heavy security and enter the building are being tried in their absence.
Ozdemir Sabanci was the youngest of five brothers of the Sabanci family, an industrial dynasty with interests rangeing from cars to textiles and processed foods.
